name: Denisova 3
description: Distal manual phalanx of a young female. This is the type specimen for the Denisovan genome: a low-coverage nuclear genome in Reich et al. 2010 and a high-coverage genome in Meyer et al. 2012.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by nuclear DNA from the specimen itself.

name: Denisova 4
description: Upper molar whose mitochondrial genome is highly similar to that of the Denisova 3 finger bone.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by mitochondrial DNA from the tooth.

name: Denisova 8
description: Upper molar. Sawyer et al. 2015 recovered its mitochondrial genome and a low-coverage nuclear genome.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by DNA from the tooth.

name: Denisova 2
dateLabel: Among the oldest Denisova Cave hominin fossils
description: Deciduous molar. Slon et al. 2017 recovered a mitochondrial genome and placed the tooth in the Denisovan clade.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by mitochondrial DNA from the tooth.

name: Denisova 11 (Denny)
description: Long-bone fragment from a girl whose mother was a Neanderthal and whose father was a Denisovan.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by a nuclear genome from the fragment. The genome is first-generation hybrid, so the specimen is labeled as both Denisovan and Neanderthal.

name: Denisova Cave sediments
description: Sediment samples from the cave contain Denisovan mitochondrial DNA. This is site evidence, not a fossil of a named individual.
gradeRationale: Confirmed Denisovan mitochondrial DNA from the sediments. It does not by itself identify a particular bone.

name: Xiahe 1
description: Partial mandible from Baishiya Karst Cave. No DNA was recovered. Ancient proteins place it with Denisovans, and the mandible is dated by uranium-series on carbonate to at least 160,000 years.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics that Chen et al. 2019 place with the Denisovan genome. A surface scan is available from the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology after registration; it is not copied into this site.

image.caption: Xiahe mandible surface scan
image.license: MPI EVA download. Registration required. Not redistributed here.

name: Xiahe 2
dateLabel: Late Pleistocene, within a cave sequence from about 160,000 to 45,000 years ago
description: Rib fragment. Shotgun proteomics recovered a much larger Denisovan-matching proteome than Xiahe 1 and places Xiahe 2 with the high-coverage Denisova 3 genome.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics in Xia et al. 2024.

name: Baishiya Karst Cave sediments
description: Denisovan mitochondrial DNA from cave sediments. This is site evidence, not a fossil of a named individual.
gradeRationale: Confirmed Denisovan mitochondrial DNA from the sediments (Zhang et al. 2020).

name: Penghu 1
dateLabel: Pleistocene; direct uranium dating was unsuccessful
description: Male mandible dredged by a fishing net from the Penghu Channel. Chang et al. 2015 described the fossil. DNA extraction has failed. Proteins recovered later include a collagen variant shared with Denisova 3, Xiahe 1, and Xiahe 2.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics in Tsutaya et al. 2025. The earlier morphological description alone did not establish that grade.

name: Harbin cranium
description: Nearly complete cranium, previously named Homo longi. Ninety-five endogenous proteins include a reliable Denisovan-derived collagen variant, and the proteome clusters with Denisova 3. Mitochondrial DNA from dental calculus of the same individual falls in the Denisovan clade.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by both palaeoproteomics and mitochondrial DNA from the specimen. The earlier species name Homo longi is kept as the morphological assignment that the molecular results reidentify.

name: BFD767
description: Parietal fragment from Bianfu Cave.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics. Rao et al. 2026 report the Denisovan-specific collagen variant COL1A2 R996K and a phylogeny that groups the specimen with Denisova 3.

name: BFD769
description: Parietal fragment from Bianfu Cave.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics, including COL1A2 R996K, in Rao et al. 2026.

name: BFD771
description: Proximal radius, the first Denisovan radius identified by proteins.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics, including COL1A2 R996K, in Rao et al. 2026.

name: YHB3518
description: Tooth. Enamel proteins include the amelogenin Y isoform, so this individual was male.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics, including COL1A2 R996K, in Rao et al. 2026.

name: YHB3075
description: Tooth. Enamel proteins include the amelogenin Y isoform, so this individual was male.
gradeRationale: Confirmed by palaeoproteomics, including COL1A2 R996K, in Rao et al. 2026.

name: TNH2-1
description: Unerupted lower molar of a young individual, probably female. The crown is morphometrically closest to the molars of the Xiahe 1 mandible. Enamel proteins identify the genus Homo and do not provide a Denisovan-specific sequence.
gradeRationale: Demeter et al. 2022 argue that a Denisovan assignment is the most parsimonious morphological hypothesis. Tsutaya et al. 2025 still list it among candidates that lack Denisovan DNA or Denisovan-specific proteins. That is the likely grade: the authors' attribution, without a Denisovan biomolecule.

name: Xujiayao hominin remains
dateLabel: Late Middle to early Late Pleistocene
description: A scattered series of cranial and dental fragments from Locality 74093, including a maxilla, parietal pieces, and isolated teeth. No Denisovan DNA or Denisovan proteins have been reported from them.
gradeRationale: Possible because Demeter et al. 2022 and Tsutaya et al. 2025 cite Xujiayao among East Asian fossils suggested as Denisovan on morphology, including traits predicted from Denisovan methylation. Both discussions treat that suggestion as unconfirmed.

name: Xuchang 1
description: Archaic human cranium from Lingjing, described by Li et al. 2017. The description paper does not identify it as Denisovan.
gradeRationale: Possible only. Later papers, including Demeter et al. 2022 and Tsutaya et al. 2025, list Xuchang among morphological candidates. There is no Denisovan DNA or protein from the cranium.

name: Xuchang 2
description: Second archaic cranium from Lingjing, described with Xuchang 1.
gradeRationale: Possible only, on the same morphological candidacy as Xuchang 1. No Denisovan DNA or protein has been reported.
